title: Commissioner's memorandum (invented practice source)
text: Merehaven, 18 March 1812. The dockside families are idle and untrustworthy by habit. Their agitation comes from an aversion to work, not from distress. The new quay levy merely applies ordinary arrangements. There is no reason to suspend immediate collection. I have not inspected the payroll books, but the petitioners' conduct confirms my assessment.
author: Commissioner Vale (invented)
perspective: A prejudiced official account defending collection; its generalizations are assertions to examine, not established descriptions of workers.
locator: Invented exercise, document A, complete text
purpose: Defend immediate collection after a protest
context: All people, places, dates and events in this dossier are invented for software practice.

title: North Quay payroll register (invented practice source)
text: 3 March 1812. Twenty-two named North Quay workers each have twenty certified workdays entered for February. Payment of February wages is postponed pending a treasury remittance. 10 March: quay levy notices served, with full payment due on 13 March. February wages remained unpaid on 14 March. This register records certified work and amounts due; it does not record household savings or income from other employment.
author: North Quay payroll clerk (invented)
perspective: An administrative record with a narrow accounting purpose; its coverage of workers and household resources is limited.
locator: Invented exercise, document B, complete text
purpose: Record certified work, wages due and collection notices
context: Entirely invented. Relationships with the other records have not been established except where explicitly stated.

title: Town notice reprinting the memorandum (invented practice source)
text: Town notice, 20 March 1812. The following is reproduced from Commissioner Vale's memorandum of 18 March: The dockside families are idle and untrustworthy by habit. Their agitation comes from an aversion to work, not from distress. The printer has added no observations of the workers, their employment or the gathering.
author: Merehaven town printer (invented)
perspective: A transmission of the commissioner's account, not another witness to the events.
locator: Invented exercise, document C, complete text
context: Entirely invented. Its dependence on document A is explicit; the shared independence_group records that relationship.

title: Workers' petition for installments (invented practice source)
text: 11 March 1812. We, eleven signatories working at North Quay, ask that the quay levy be collected in installments. We have continued our work while waiting for February wages. Several of us have borrowed for food. We ask for a public schedule of collection and payment. These are our complaints; the petition does not speak for every household in Merehaven.
author: Eleven petition signatories (invented)
perspective: An advocacy document seeking relief; its claims and representativeness require assessment.
locator: Invented exercise, document D, complete text
purpose: Request installment payments and a public schedule
context: Entirely invented. No information about who drafted the wording or how the signatories were selected is supplied.

title: Clerk's filings and arrest book (invented practice source)
text: 12 March 1812. A group at the quay gate delivered a request about the levy and unpaid wages. The request was entered among the day's filings. No arrests are entered for 12 March. This book contains filings received and arrests processed by this office; it does not provide a continuous account of activity at the quay.
author: Local court clerk (invented)
perspective: An administrative register with limited recording scope; silence about an event is not a full account of what happened.
locator: Invented exercise, document E, complete text
purpose: Register filings and arrests processed by the office
context: Entirely invented. The completeness of other offices' records is unknown.

title: Hill Parish installment roll (invented practice source)
text: Hill Parish, March 1812. The new levy is divided into three monthly installments. The roll lists scheduled collection dates and receipts. It contains no entries for wages owed, household savings, public meetings or informal complaints. The Merehaven quay payroll is not part of this roll.
author: Hill Parish collection clerk (invented)
perspective: A comparison record showing a different payment arrangement, with too little information to hold other conditions constant.
locator: Invented exercise, document F, complete text
context: Entirely invented. The packet supplies no basis for treating this parish as an otherwise identical comparison group.
